requirements.quote:
The primary goal of TLS is to provide a secure channel between two
   communicating peers; the only requirement from the underlying
   transport is a reliable, in-order data stream.
requirements.condition: when TLS is used over an underlying transport
requirements.required_behavior: use a transport that provides a reliable, in-order data stream
requirements.why_checkable: The transport integration can be inspected or exercised to verify reliable, ordered byte delivery.

requirements.quote:
Authentication: The server side of the channel is always
      authenticated; the client side is optionally authenticated.
requirements.required_behavior: authenticate the server side of the channel
requirements.forbidden_behavior: establish the channel without authenticating the server side
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake completion paths can be checked to ensure server authentication is established.

requirements.quote:
Authentication: The server side of the channel is always
      authenticated; the client side is optionally authenticated.
requirements.condition: when client authentication is not selected
requirements.required_behavior: allow the client side of the channel to remain unauthenticated
requirements.forbidden_behavior: require client authentication for every TLS channel
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake state paths can be tested with and without client authentication.

requirements.quote:
Confidentiality: Data sent over the channel after establishment is
      only visible to the endpoints.
requirements.condition: after the TLS channel is established
requirements.required_behavior: protect channel data so that its contents are visible only to the endpoints
requirements.forbidden_behavior: expose application data in plaintext to a non-endpoint
requirements.why_checkable: Captured post-establishment traffic can be checked for plaintext disclosure and successful endpoint-only decryption.

requirements.quote:
TLS does not hide the length of
      the data it transmits, though endpoints are able to pad TLS
      records in order to obscure lengths and improve protection against
      traffic analysis techniques.
requirements.condition: when an endpoint chooses to obscure transmitted lengths
requirements.required_behavior: allow the endpoint to pad TLS records
requirements.why_checkable: Record construction and parsing can be tested with permitted padding.

requirements.quote:
Integrity: Data sent over the channel after establishment cannot
      be modified by attackers without detection.
requirements.condition: after the TLS channel is established
requirements.required_behavior: detect attacker modification of channel data
requirements.forbidden_behavior: accept modified protected data as authentic
requirements.why_checkable: Tampering with protected records can be tested to verify that modification is detected.

requirements.quote:
The handshake
      protocol is designed to resist tampering; an active attacker
      should not be able to force the peers to negotiate different
      parameters than they would if the connection were not under
      attack.
requirements.condition: when an active attacker tampers with the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: preserve the negotiated parameters that the peers would select without the attack
requirements.forbidden_behavior: allow the attacker to force different negotiated parameters
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake mutation and downgrade tests can compare negotiated parameters with an untampered baseline.

requirements.quote:
A record protocol (Section 5) that uses the parameters established
      by the handshake protocol to protect traffic between the
      communicating peers.
requirements.required_behavior: use the parameters established by the handshake protocol
requirements.forbidden_behavior: protect traffic with parameters inconsistent with the handshake
requirements.why_checkable: Record-layer configuration can be compared directly with the negotiated handshake state.

requirements.quote:
The record protocol divides traffic up into
      a series of records, each of which is independently protected
      using the traffic keys.
requirements.condition: when the record protocol sends traffic
requirements.required_behavior: divide the traffic into a series of records
requirements.why_checkable: Record serialization can be inspected to verify that traffic is framed as TLS records.

requirements.quote:
The record protocol divides traffic up into
      a series of records, each of which is independently protected
      using the traffic keys.
requirements.condition: for each record produced by the record protocol
requirements.required_behavior: protect the record independently using the traffic keys
requirements.forbidden_behavior: emit an unprotected record where protected traffic is required
requirements.why_checkable: Individual records can be decrypted and tampered with to verify per-record protection under the traffic keys.

requirements.quote:
While TLS 1.3 is not directly
   compatible with previous versions, all versions of TLS incorporate a
   versioning mechanism which allows clients and servers to
   interoperably negotiate a common version if one is supported by both
   peers.
requirements.condition: when the client and server both support a common TLS version
requirements.required_behavior: use the TLS versioning mechanism to negotiate that common version interoperably
requirements.why_checkable: Version-negotiation tests can offer intersecting version sets and verify the selected common version.

requirements.quote:
Authentication can happen via asymmetric cryptography (e.g., RSA
      [RSA], the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)
      [ECDSA], or the Edwards-Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (EdDSA)
      [RFC8032]) or a symmetric pre-shared key (PSK).
requirements.required_behavior: use asymmetric cryptography or a symmetric pre-shared key as the authentication basis
requirements.why_checkable: Negotiated authentication paths can be classified as asymmetric-signature or PSK based.

requirements.quote:
These properties should be true even in the face of an attacker who
   has complete control of the network, as described in [RFC3552].
requirements.condition: when an attacker has complete control of the network
requirements.required_behavior: preserve server authentication and the selected client-authentication semantics
requirements.forbidden_behavior: allow network control to bypass endpoint authentication
requirements.why_checkable: Active interception and credential-substitution tests can exercise the adjacent authentication property under the stated attacker model.

requirements.quote:
These properties should be true even in the face of an attacker who
   has complete control of the network, as described in [RFC3552].
requirements.condition: when an attacker has complete control of the network
requirements.forbidden_behavior: expose protected channel data to the network attacker
requirements.why_checkable: Traffic interception tests can exercise the adjacent confidentiality property under the stated attacker model.

requirements.quote:
These properties should be true even in the face of an attacker who
   has complete control of the network, as described in [RFC3552].
requirements.condition: when an attacker has complete control of the network
requirements.required_behavior: detect modifications to protected channel data
requirements.why_checkable: Active record-tampering tests can exercise the adjacent integrity property under the stated attacker model.

requirements.quote:
A handshake protocol (Section 4) that authenticates the
      communicating parties, negotiates cryptographic modes and
      parameters, and establishes shared keying material.
requirements.required_behavior: negotiate the cryptographic modes and parameters
requirements.why_checkable: The completed handshake state can be checked for concrete negotiated algorithms and parameters.

requirements.quote:
A handshake protocol (Section 4) that authenticates the
      communicating parties, negotiates cryptographic modes and
      parameters, and establishes shared keying material.
requirements.required_behavior: establish shared keying material for the peers
requirements.why_checkable: Both peers' derived secrets can be compared for agreement after the handshake.
